title: Existence as the Total
summary: There is nothing outside existence. The universe is everything that exists.

lessons.title: Nothing outside
lessons.objective: State that there is nothing outside existence: whatever is, is inside existence.

exercises.prompt: What sits outside existence?

choices.text: Nothing
A larger empty void
A second realm of non-being
A frame that holds existence in place

feedback.note: There is nothing outside existence. Anything that is, is already inside it.

exercises.prompt: If something exists, where does it belong?

choices.text: Inside existence
Beside existence, as a neighbor
Before existence, as a prior stage
After existence, once the total ends

feedback.note: To be at all is to be inside existence. There is no outside slot for a real thing.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the verdict this lesson gives it.

feedback.note: The outside of existence does not contain a further something. What exists is inside the total.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s first line.

feedback.note: The line is nothing outside existence, not nothing inside it.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states this lesson.

feedback.note: Nothing is outside existence. Inside and consciousness are not the words this line needs.

exercises.prompt: Someone says a hidden world lies beyond everything that is. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: If it is, it is already inside existence
It is too small to count as real
Only a vote can place it outside
It counts only after people notice it

feedback.note: A hidden world that exists is not outside existence. Existing puts it in the total.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it names here.

feedback.note: Existence already includes whatever is. A further realm beyond it does not add a real outside.

exercises.prompt: Finish the rule about anything that is.

feedback.note: Being puts a thing inside existence. Outside, before, and beside are the wrong locations.

lessons.title: Everything that exists
lessons.objective: Define the universe as everything that exists, not as one object among other objects.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is the universe?

choices.text: Everything that exists
One large object among many
Only the sky above the earth
Only what a mind is thinking now

feedback.note: The universe is everything that exists. It is the total, not one item in a longer list.

exercises.prompt: Which description treats the universe as a member of a larger set?

choices.text: One thing that sits next to other totalities
The sum of all that exists
The whole of existence
All existents taken together

feedback.note: Calling the universe one member beside other totalities shrinks it. The universe is the sum, not a member.

exercises.prompt: Match each name to the role this lesson gives it.

feedback.note: Single existents are parts. There is not a second universe outside the one total of what exists.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s second line.

feedback.note: The universe is everything that exists, not nothing, not one thing, and not a wish.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition of the universe.

feedback.note: The universe is everything that exists. A planet or a container is not that definition.

exercises.prompt: A star, a person, and a fact all exist. How do they stand to the universe?

choices.text: They are included in the total
Each is a rival universe
They stand outside the universe
They count only if someone lists them

feedback.note: Whatever exists is part of the universe. Listing it does not decide whether it is in the total.

exercises.prompt: Match the wording to the idea it teaches.

feedback.note: The universe is the sum of existents. Treating it as one object among others leaves existents out.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

parts.text: , not one member of a larger set.

feedback.note: Sum is the right word. Member, wish, and void all miss the total.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps the universe as the total?

choices.text: The universe is everything that exists
The universe is a box with an outside
The universe is half of what exists
The universe is only an idea of a total

feedback.note: Half, a box with an outside, and a mere idea all cut the universe down. It is everything that exists.

lessons.title: Nonexistence is not a place
lessons.objective: Reject treating nonexistence as a region, a background, or a somewhere beyond what exists.

exercises.prompt: What is nonexistence, on this lesson’s terms?

choices.text: Not a place where things can be
A distant country past the last star
An empty room behind the universe
The stage on which existence stands

feedback.note: Nonexistence is not a region. A country, a room, or a stage would already be something that exists.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t you point to a background of nothing?

choices.text: A background you can point to would exist
Nothing is only the color black
Nothing is only what is very far away
Nothing is only what makes no sound

feedback.note: Distance, darkness, and silence are still features of what exists. A real background is not nonexistence.

exercises.prompt: Match each picture to the correction.

feedback.note: Real empty space exists, so it is not nonexistence. Nonexistence is not a background you can travel to.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejection.

feedback.note: Place is the word to reject. A fact, an existent, or the sum would already be something that is.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that blocks the picture of a somewhere.

feedback.note: Nonexistence is not a place. Calling it a room or the universe would turn it into something that is.

exercises.prompt: A story says the hero leaves existence and enters the land of nothing. What does this lesson say?

choices.text: There is no such land to enter
The land is on the far side of the map
The land opens only while people sleep
The land exists if enough readers agree

feedback.note: A land you could enter would exist. Nonexistence is not a destination beyond the total.

exercises.prompt: Which item is still inside existence?

choices.text: A real gap between two stars
A beyond that contains nothing that is
An outside of existence
A nowhere that is a region

feedback.note: A real gap is part of what exists. An outside, a beyond, or a nowhere-as-region is the picture to drop.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

feedback.note: Whatever is real exists. That keeps it out of the role of nonexistence.

exercises.prompt: Sort the phrases.

feedback.note: Darkness and silence can be real features. A realm of nonexistence cannot be a region beyond them.

lessons.title: No larger container
lessons.objective: See that existence is not inside a bigger frame, void, or second total.

exercises.prompt: What contains existence?

choices.text: Nothing larger contains it
An outer void
A frame around the universe
A second, bigger totality

feedback.note: Existence is the total. A void, a frame, or a second totality would have to be outside it, and nothing is.

exercises.prompt: Why does a bigger frame fail?

choices.text: If the frame is, it is already in existence
The frame would be too heavy to hold
Frames only work when nobody sees them
A frame can be added after the facts

feedback.note: A real frame exists, so it cannot sit outside existence as a container for the total.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed container to the result.

feedback.note: Anything large enough to contain the total is not outside the total. Existence is already the whole.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about a container.

feedback.note: The mistake is a larger container. Smaller, mental, and chosen do not name that mistake.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that rejects a second total.

feedback.note: There is no second totality. Extra universes or an outer frame would still have to fall inside existence.

exercises.prompt: A model draws a circle around the universe and labels the margin outside. What is the error?

choices.text: The margin pretends something contains the total
Circles cannot be drawn in ink
The circle is drawn at the wrong scale
Only the word universe may be labeled

feedback.note: A margin around the universe suggests a container. Nothing outside existence supplies that container.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the answer.

feedback.note: The three answers are one claim: the total has no outside and no bigger holder.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two blanks.

parts.text: A second total would still be

feedback.note: More being is more existence. It does not create an outside.

lessons.title: Hold the two lines
lessons.objective: Hold both lines together: nothing is outside existence, and the universe is everything that exists.

exercises.prompt: Which pair is this unit’s whole claim?

choices.text: Nothing outside existence, and the universe is everything that exists
Existence exists, and consciousness is conscious
Identity applied to action, and entities act
Facts that are, and facts that choice brings about

feedback.note: This unit’s two lines are about the total. The other pairs belong to other units.

exercises.prompt: How do the two lines relate?

choices.text: They state one total in two ways
They compete, and only one can be kept
The second cancels the first
Either line may be dropped

feedback.note: Nothing outside existence is the same claim as the universe being everything that exists.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to the mistake it blocks.

pairs.left: The universe is everything that exists
pairs.right: The universe as one object among others

feedback.note: Each line blocks a way of shrinking or surrounding the total. Together they leave no outside.

exercises.prompt: Restore both lines.

feedback.note: The two words are existence and exists. Consciousness and wishes are not this unit’s pair.

exercises.prompt: Build the combined claim.

feedback.note: The universe is all of existence. Half, or a place outside, cuts the total.

exercises.prompt: Which addition would break the unit?

choices.text: A something beyond everything that exists
There is nothing outside existence
The universe is everything that exists
Whatever is, is in the total

feedback.note: A something beyond everything that exists contradicts both lines. The other three keep the total.

exercises.prompt: Match the short label to the full line.

pairs.right: The universe is everything that exists

feedback.note: No outside and the sum are the two lines. Held together, they are one claim about the total.

exercises.prompt: Order the words that close the unit.

feedback.note: Nothing lies outside the universe, because the universe is everything that exists.

exercises.prompt: A learner remembers only one line. Which reminder keeps the unit whole?

choices.text: Keep both: no outside, and the universe is the sum
Drop the universe and keep only a void
Swap the universe for one object in a list
Add a container and keep the rest

feedback.note: The unit is both lines. A void, a single object, or a container leaves the total incomplete.

exercises.prompt: Close with the summary.

parts.text: There is nothing outside existence. The

feedback.note: Universe is the word that names everything that exists. Void, frame, and wish do not.
